approachQuestion.prompt: Given a lowercase string s and integer 3 <= k <= 200,000, repeatedly delete any k adjacent equal letters until no such run remains. Deleted runs may expose new runs. Length<=200,000. Example s="aabbbbaa", k=4 -> "".

options.text: Keep groups (letter,count) for the reduced prefix. Extend the top group for a matching letter; when count reaches k remove it. Later letters can then extend the newly exposed group.
options.feedback: A count below k must stay unresolved. In aabbbbaa with k=4, deleting bbbb exposes aaaa and deleting that group leaves the empty string.

options.text: Identify every run of length at least k in the original string, delete those runs once, and return the remaining characters.
options.feedback: In aabbbbaa with k=4, deleting bbbb exposes aaaa, which must also be deleted; a single original pass leaves an invalid result.

options.text: Count each letter globally and keep characters whose total count is not divisible by k.
options.feedback: Counts ignore adjacency: separated copies cannot combine into one removable run.

options.text: Find the leftmost k equal adjacent letters, delete exactly those k, shift the suffix, and restart; return when no such group remains.
options.feedback: This implements repeated deletion correctly but repeatedly scans and shifts text instead of retaining the letter and multiplicity at each unresolved boundary.

Deleting a completed group exposes the previous group for later letters. Store counts below k until that point; deleting every repeated pair would implement a different rule when k is greater than two.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For threshold-adjacent-run-removal-optimal, let n be the number of input operations or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: The input is immutable; returned output is excluded from auxiliary space. All stack operations and value comparisons take constant time.
The algorithm is iterative with O(1) call-stack use. The auxiliary stack may hold up to n fixed-size entries.
No hashing, recursion, or hidden array copy occurs. Any movement between stacks counts as constant time per item.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each character updates one group, with linear total group removal and copying.
details: Each letter increments one top group or creates one; a deletion removes a completed group once. Group counts are bounded by k-1. At most n groups remain, and copying surviving characters costs at most linear time. Total time and auxiliary space are O(n).
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: An alternating-letter input retains a linear number of unresolved groups because no group reaches k.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each character increments one group and each deleted group was created earlier; deletions do not trigger a fresh whole-string pass.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A final character may complete a group of k and expose another merge, so every character may affect the answer.
